summary: 2024 facility ban expanded in 2026 to colleges and universities, raising its tier to “Worst Laws Passed” in the July 2026 assessment; part of the 18-state birth-sex-definition group. Below the national score 0.36.

sources.summary: Erin In The Morning, 'Anti-Trans National Legal Risk Assessment Map: July 2026' (Stonewall News, published 27 Aug 2026): per-state legal-risk grading; records South Carolina rising from 'High Risk' to 'Worst Laws Passed' after its bathroom ban was expanded to colleges and universities, and lists SC among 'The Worst States (AL, AR, IA, IN, LA, MS, OH, OK, ND, SC, SD, TN, UT, WV, WY)' on the adult map, under a national frame of 'Worst Policies In Effect'.

ACLU of South Carolina statement on Governor Henry McMaster signing House Bill 4756: the law requires transgender students in South Carolina public schools and universities to use restrooms and changing facilities that do not match their gender. ACLU-SC executive director Jace Woodrum (the state's first openly transgender ACLU affiliate director) condemns the bill as treating trans youth as outcasts and notes lawmakers rejected single-user-stall alternatives framed as privacy fixes.
